title: Project 2025 tax proposal leaves treatment of CTC and EITC unclear
description_medium: In August 2024, Democratic staff of the Joint Economic Committee examined Project 2025’s proposal to remove most tax deductions, credits and exclusions. The plan did not say whether the Child Tax Credit or Earned Income Tax Credit would be retained, leaving their future treatment unclear.
description_long: In August 2024, Democratic staff of the Joint Economic Committee analyzed Project 2025’s proposed tax changes. The plan called for a simplified individual tax system and removal of most deductions, credits and exclusions, but did not specify whether the Child Tax Credit or Earned Income Tax Credit would remain. The committee’s analysis described these credits as important to low- and middle-income households and modeled higher tax burdens for families if the credits were eliminated. It also projected lower taxes for some high-income households under the plan’s proposed rate structure. Those estimates depended on changes that Congress had not enacted. The briefing therefore raised questions about how the broad proposal would treat family tax benefits; it did not document a Trump administration repeal of either credit.

corrected_wording.proposed: Project 2025 tax proposal leaves treatment of CTC and EITC unclear
corrected_wording.reason: The JEC analysis describes a proposal that leaves two named credits unspecified; the rewrite presents projected effects conditionally and removes the false claim that Trump had eliminated them.

source_access_notes: Read the Joint Economic Committee Democrats’ August 1, 2024 issue brief and its description of the Mandate for Leadership tax proposal.
blockers: Project 2025 does not specify whether CTC and EITC would be retained, so their treatment under the proposal cannot be stated definitively.
rationale: The JEC analysis describes a proposal that leaves two named credits unspecified; the rewrite presents projected effects conditionally and removes the false claim that Trump had eliminated them.

title: Ricardo Bellino pitches Trump on Villa Trump, an unbuilt São Paulo resort
description_medium: Brazilian entrepreneur Ricardo Bellino pitched Donald Trump in 2003 on Villa Trump, a proposed golf and residential resort near São Paulo. Bellino later valued the plan at $500 million. Investors withdrew, the resort was never built, and Business Day reported that Trump and Bellino received termination fees.
description_long: Brazilian entrepreneur Ricardo Bellino said he pitched Donald Trump in 2003 on a branded golf and residential development near São Paulo. Bellino later called the proposal Villa Trump and valued the planned resort at $500 million. Business Day reported that the concept included a Jack Nicklaus-designed golf course and that the deal fell through after Brazilian investors backed out. The proposed development never reached construction. Bellino’s later account described termination fees paid after the project ended, including $7 million to Trump and twice that amount to Bellino and his partners.

corrected_wording.proposed: Ricardo Bellino pitches Trump on Villa Trump, an unbuilt São Paulo resort
corrected_wording.reason: Business Day reports both that the resort was never built and that Trump received termination fees; the revised title and copy distinguish the pitch from the later ended deal.

source_access_notes: Read Business Day’s interview with Ricardo Bellino, including its account of the pitch, investor withdrawal and termination fees.
blockers: Business Day reports the pitch and termination fees but does not reproduce a signed development agreement or substantiate the original title’s claim about Bellino’s associate.
rationale: Business Day reports both that the resort was never built and that Trump received termination fees; the revised title and copy distinguish the pitch from the later ended deal.

title: The Apprentice premieres on NBC with Donald Trump as host
description_medium: NBC premiered The Apprentice on January 8, 2004. Created by Mark Burnett, the reality series put 16 contestants through business competitions for a job with Donald Trump. Burnett’s earlier Russia-linked reality concept involved the Mir space station; it was separate from this NBC show. The premiere presented the contest as a 13-week job interview.
description_long: The Apprentice debuted on NBC on January 8, 2004, with Donald Trump as its host and Mark Burnett as its creator and executive producer. The first season placed 16 contestants in business competitions for a job with Trump, and each episode ended with him dismissing one participant. NBC promoted the show as a 13-week job interview, with New York City serving as the contestants’ “real jungle.” The format brought Trump’s real-estate persona to a national television audience and made his boardroom catchphrase part of the program’s identity. Burnett’s earlier concept, Destination: Mir, concerned contestants training for a possible trip to Russia’s space station and was unrelated to The Apprentice. The series developed by Burnett and NBC became one of Trump’s most prominent entertainment roles before his presidential campaigns. The first season’s winner was offered a $250,000 position in Trump’s organization.

corrected_wording.proposed: The Apprentice premieres on NBC with Donald Trump as host
corrected_wording.reason: The premiere coverage identifies Burnett’s role and the show’s format; the separate Destination: Mir proposal explains why the original Putin characterization does not describe The Apprentice.

source_access_notes: Read Washington Post premiere-week coverage and separate reporting on Burnett’s earlier Destination: Mir concept.
rationale: The premiere coverage identifies Burnett’s role and the show’s format; the separate Destination: Mir proposal explains why the original Putin characterization does not describe The Apprentice.

title: J.D. Vance starts Iraq deployment blog under the name “JD Hamel”
description_medium: During his 2005 deployment to Iraq, Marine J.D. Vance began a blog called The Ruminations of JD Hamel, using the name he then went by. In one post, Vance described leaving his family to deploy. Vance later wrote a separate blog while attending Yale Law School.
description_long: J.D. Vance began The Ruminations of JD Hamel in 2005 while deployed to Iraq as a Marine. He wrote under the name JD Hamel, which he used at the time, and posted personal reflections during the deployment. In one post about leaving his family for Iraq, he wrote that the departure had been emotional. His posts are an early personal record from before he became a writer, Ohio senator and Donald Trump’s running mate. It is distinct from The Hillbilly Elite, the later blog he wrote while attending Yale Law School. The Iraq blog is thus an early personal record from his military service, with posts about family, films such as Garden State, and deployment. His later posts reflected his experience in law school and public life as a student.

corrected_wording.proposed: J.D. Vance starts Iraq deployment blog under the name “JD Hamel”
corrected_wording.reason: The Guardian dates the Iraq deployment blog to 2005 and distinguishes it from Vance’s Yale-era blog; the assigned July 11 date remains unverified.

source_access_notes: Read the Guardian’s review of Vance’s 2005 Iraq blog and its comparison with his later Yale blog.
blockers: The Guardian dates the blog to Vance’s 2005 deployment but does not verify the entry’s assigned July 11 start date.
rationale: The Guardian dates the Iraq deployment blog to 2005 and distinguishes it from Vance’s Yale-era blog; the assigned July 11 date remains unverified.

title: Barron William Trump is born in New York on March 20, 2006
description_medium: Melania Trump gave birth to Barron William Trump in New York on March 20, 2006. Donald Trump announced the birth in an MSNBC telephone interview about 20 minutes later, saying mother and baby were doing well. Barron was Donald Trump’s fifth child and Melania’s first.
description_long: Barron William Trump was born in New York on March 20, 2006, to Donald and Melania Trump. Donald Trump announced the birth in a telephone interview with MSNBC’s Imus in the Morning about 20 minutes after the baby arrived, saying, “Everyone’s perfect.” The child was Donald Trump’s fifth and Melania Trump’s first. Associated Press reports said Melania, then 35, had been in labor for eight hours. The couple had announced the pregnancy months earlier. The birth made Barron the youngest of Donald Trump’s five children and the couple’s only child together.

corrected_wording.proposed: Barron William Trump is born in New York on March 20, 2006
corrected_wording.reason: CBS/AP and its contemporaneous syndication establish the date, family relationships and announcement; the copy avoids adding later biographical details unrelated to the birth.

source_access_notes: Read CBS/AP’s March 2006 birth report and a contemporaneous AP syndication for birth and family details.
blockers: The contemporaneous birth reports provide the announcement and family details but little further information about the delivery or hospital.
rationale: CBS/AP and its contemporaneous syndication establish the date, family relationships and announcement; the copy avoids adding later biographical details unrelated to the birth.

title: Trump unveils Trump SoHo project with Bayrock Group in 2006
description_medium: Donald Trump unveiled the Trump SoHo hotel-condominium project during The Apprentice’s June 2006 season finale. The development was a partnership with Bayrock Group, whose principals included Tevfik Arif and Felix Sater. Sater had pleaded guilty in an earlier securities-fraud case; the project announcement itself was a real-estate launch.
description_long: Donald Trump unveiled Trump SoHo during The Apprentice’s June 2006 season finale, presenting the Manhattan hotel-condominium as a new development. The project involved the Trump Organization, Bayrock Group and the Sapir Organization. Bayrock principals Tevfik Arif and Felix Sater joined the partnership; Sater had pleaded guilty in 1998 to a racketeering charge connected to a securities-fraud scheme and later cooperated with authorities. The building opened in 2010. Years later, Manhattan prosecutors investigated whether Donald Trump Jr. and Ivanka Trump had misled buyers about sales figures. A New Yorker investigation reported that prosecutors considered indictments but the district attorney ultimately closed the case without charges.

corrected_wording.proposed: Trump unveils Trump SoHo project with Bayrock Group in 2006
corrected_wording.reason: The New Yorker and ProPublica connect the project to Bayrock and document later scrutiny of sales representations; the revised event copy distinguishes that scrutiny from the 2006 launch.

source_access_notes: Read ProPublica’s Trump SoHo partnership account and the New Yorker’s report on the later Manhattan buyer investigation.
blockers: The records cited for the launch do not establish criminal conduct by Trump; later reporting on the buyer investigation concerns his adult children and was closed without charges.
rationale: The New Yorker and ProPublica connect the project to Bayrock and document later scrutiny of sales representations; the revised event copy distinguishes that scrutiny from the 2006 launch.

title: Trump executive order seeks to restrict federal support for gender-affirming care for youth
description_medium: On January 28, 2025, Donald Trump signed an executive order titled “Protecting Children from Chemical and Surgical Mutilation,” directing agencies to restrict federal funding and health-program support for gender-affirming care for people under 19. Human Rights Watch documented clinic service interruptions and lawsuits challenging the policy.
description_long: On January 28, 2025, President Donald Trump signed an executive order titled “Protecting Children from Chemical and Surgical Mutilation.” It directed agencies to restrict federal funding and health-program support for gender-affirming care for people under 19 and to investigate providers. Human Rights Watch reported that clinics suspended or reduced some services amid uncertainty about the order’s reach. Legal challenges followed, and the federal policy was not fully enforced. The order came as state bans and litigation were already affecting access to care. The order came as state bans and litigation were already affecting access to care. In the following months, some clinics suspended or reduced services amid uncertainty about federal funding and investigations.

corrected_wording.proposed: Trump executive order seeks to restrict federal support for gender-affirming care for youth
corrected_wording.reason: Human Rights Watch documents the order’s funding and program mechanisms, clinic interruptions and litigation; the revised copy reports those consequences without repeating unsupported claims of federal criminalization.

source_access_notes: Read Human Rights Watch’s June 2025 report on the January order, clinic effects and legal challenges.
blockers: The June 2025 HRW report documents interrupted services and ongoing legal challenges but does not establish a settled nationwide effect or the disposition of every case.
rationale: Human Rights Watch documents the order’s funding and program mechanisms, clinic interruptions and litigation; the revised copy reports those consequences without repeating unsupported claims of federal criminalization.

title: Breitbart Jerusalem launches as a bureau and content vertical in November 2015
description_medium: Breitbart News launched a Jerusalem bureau and content vertical on November 17, 2015, with Aaron Klein as bureau chief. The opening followed Breitbart London’s 2014 launch. CEO Larry Solov later recalled that he and founder Andrew Breitbart had discussed creating the parent network during a 2007 trip to Israel.
description_long: Breitbart News announced the launch of Breitbart Jerusalem on November 17, 2015, describing it as a new bureau and content vertical. The announced bureau would cover Israel and other Middle Eastern countries, and named Aaron Klein as bureau chief. Klein had previously led WND.com’s Jerusalem bureau. The launch followed Breitbart London, which began in 2014, as the company expanded its international operations. A year later, Jewish Telegraphic Agency reported that CEO Larry Solov recalled discussing a new media company with founder Andrew Breitbart during a 2007 trip to Israel. His account placed the parent network’s origins during a visit eight years before the Jerusalem bureau opened. Klein later told JTA he planned to expand the Israel operation and hire more reporters. In a separate interview, he said the bureau was established to counter what he viewed as bias in other outlets’ Israel coverage.

corrected_wording.proposed: Breitbart Jerusalem launches as a bureau and content vertical in November 2015
corrected_wording.reason: The November 2015 announcement and JTA’s anniversary coverage establish the bureau’s launch and distinguish it from Solov’s account of the parent company’s earlier origins.

source_access_notes: Read JTA’s 2016 anniversary report and Breitbart’s November 2015 launch announcement.
rationale: The November 2015 announcement and JTA’s anniversary coverage establish the bureau’s launch and distinguish it from Solov’s account of the parent company’s earlier origins.

title: Michael Caputo consults for Volodymyr Lytvyn’s Ukrainian campaign in 2007
description_medium: American political consultant Michael Caputo worked on Volodymyr Lytvyn’s parliamentary campaign in Ukraine in 2007. Lytvyn had served as speaker of parliament and as chief of staff to former president Leonid Kuchma. The Kyiv Post also noted that Caputo had worked in Ukraine before the 2007 campaign.
description_long: Michael Caputo, an American political consultant, worked on Volodymyr Lytvyn’s parliamentary campaign in Ukraine in 2007. The Kyiv Post later described Lytvyn as a former speaker of parliament and former chief of staff to President Leonid Kuchma. Caputo worked with fellow Republican operative Roger Stone on the campaign. Caputo later returned to U.S. politics and became associated with Donald Trump’s campaigns. Caputo’s work was consulting for a candidate in Ukraine’s 2007 parliamentary contest.

corrected_wording.proposed: Michael Caputo consults for Volodymyr Lytvyn’s Ukrainian campaign in 2007
corrected_wording.reason: Kyiv Post’s reporting supports Caputo’s 2007 work for Lytvyn and identifies the campaign setting; its account does not support the original Putin-directed characterization.

source_access_notes: Read Kyiv Post’s report on Caputo’s work for Lytvyn’s 2007 campaign and the campaign’s contemporaneous context.
blockers: Kyiv Post identifies Caputo’s work for Lytvyn and the campaign context; it does not establish Putin’s direction or the asserted political takeover.
rationale: Kyiv Post’s reporting supports Caputo’s 2007 work for Lytvyn and identifies the campaign setting; its account does not support the original Putin-directed characterization.

title: Sergei Millian says he was involved in contract to promote Trump real estate
description_medium: In 2007, Donald Trump attended Moscow’s Millionaire Fair after Sergei Millian helped arrange the trip. Nearly a decade later, Millian told RIA Novosti he had taken part in a contract to promote Trump-branded developments in Russia and former Soviet states. He also described Russian buyers purchasing Trump-branded apartments in the United States.
description_long: Donald Trump traveled to Moscow in 2007 to attend the Millionaire Fair. Sergei Millian, then president of the Russian-American Chamber of Commerce, later told RIA Novosti that he had been involved in signing a contract to promote Trump-branded real-estate projects in Russia and other former Soviet states. Millian described himself as an exclusive broker for Trump properties. Millian also said that Russians bought apartments in Trump-branded buildings in the United States in 2007 and 2008. Michael Cohen disputed key parts of Millian’s account. No Russian project described in these accounts was built.

corrected_wording.proposed: Sergei Millian says he was involved in contract to promote Trump real estate
corrected_wording.reason: The Washington Post attributes the contract claim to Millian and reports Cohen’s dispute; the rewrite identifies what was alleged while removing the unverified earnings figure.

source_access_notes: Read the Washington Post’s reporting on Millian’s RIA Novosti interview, his contract claim and Cohen’s response.
blockers: The contract text, its terms and the claimed earnings amount are not substantiated in the reporting; the account of a business arrangement is attributed to Millian.
rationale: The Washington Post attributes the contract claim to Millian and reports Cohen’s dispute; the rewrite identifies what was alleged while removing the unverified earnings figure.
